The backend reads its port from BACKEND_PORT in .env (default 5000) and the frontend dev server from VITE_PORT (default 5173). Change either value, then restart with `./stop.sh && ./start.sh`. state.question: Summarize the inquiry report on the Ariane 5 Flight 501 failure.
state.passage:
…the launcher began to disintegrate about 39 seconds after lift-off, under aerodynamic loads from an angle of attack of more than 20 degrees. The angle came from full nozzle deflections of the boosters and the main engine, commanded by the on-board computer on the basis of data from the active inertial reference system. Those data were not flight data but a diagnostic bit pattern: the unit had shut down after a software exception. The back-up unit, running the same software, had failed in the same way one data cycle (72 milliseconds) earlier.

The exception was raised while converting a 64-bit floating-point value, the horizontal bias, to a 16-bit signed integer. The value was larger than a 16-bit integer can hold, and that conversion was one of three left unprotected. The code belonged to the alignment function, which yields meaningful results only before lift-off but kept running for about 40 seconds into flight, a carry-over from the Ariane 4 design. Ariane 5's early trajectory produces much higher horizontal velocities than Ariane 4's, so the value overflowed.

state.question: Summarize the inquiry report on the Ariane 5 Flight 501 failure.
state.passage:
A few days after landing in July 1997, the Pathfinder lander began resetting itself, and each reset cost time and some of the day's data. Engineers reproduced the fault on a copy of the flight system in the lab. A low-priority meteorological task took a mutex guarding the shared information bus; a high-priority bus management task then blocked waiting for it, and a medium-priority communications task, which needed neither, preempted the low-priority task and kept running. With the bus task stalled past its deadline, a watchdog concluded the system had hung and reset the computer.

This is priority inversion: a high-priority task left waiting on a resource held by a low-priority one, while tasks of middle priority run ahead of both. The real-time operating system offered priority inheritance, which lends the waiting task's priority to the holder until it releases the resource, but the option was off for that mutex. The team turned it on with a small patch sent to the spacecraft, and the resets stopped.

state.question: Summarize what happened to the Tacoma Narrows Bridge.
state.passage: The first Tacoma Narrows Bridge, a suspension bridge with a main span of 2,800 feet, collapsed on November 7, 1940. Its deck was a shallow plate girder only 8 feet deep, and it had moved up and down in moderate winds from the start, which earned it the nickname Galloping Gertie. On the morning of the collapse, in a steady wind of about 40 miles an hour, the vertical motion changed to a twisting one after a cable band at mid-span slipped. The twisting grew for about an hour until a section of the deck broke away and fell into the water. No person died; a dog left in a car on the deck was the only fatality. Later wind-tunnel studies put the cause down to aeroelastic flutter, a self-reinforcing interaction between the wind and the deck's own twisting, rather than simple resonance with gusts.
